error.signature: AI tells a foreigner in Chile they can get a Clave Unica (the login for most Chilean government online services) with a provisional RUN or their passport

verdict.summary: Clave Unica, issued by Chile's Servicio de Registro Civil e Identificacion, is required to use most Chilean government online services. For foreigners the only accepted credential is a valid, definitive Cedula de Identidad para Extranjeros; a provisional RUN (issued while a residency application is still processing) or a passport does not qualify, so a newly arrived resident can be blocked from Clave Unica for months while their permanent card is processed. Applicants must be 14 or older and can apply in person at a Civil Registry office, at a consulate abroad, or via a scheduled videoconference.

dead_ends.action: Tell a newcomer with a residency visa but only a provisional RUN (RUN provisorio) that they can request Clave Unica immediately
dead_ends.why_fails: Chilean immigration guides echoing Registro Civil rules state plainly that a provisional RUN cannot be used to request Clave Unica - the definitive Cedula de Identidad para Extranjeros must be issued first.
dead_ends.condition: Newly arrived foreigner still awaiting their definitive ID card

dead_ends.action: Assume a passport is an acceptable substitute for the Cedula de Identidad para Extranjeros when requesting Clave Unica
dead_ends.why_fails: La Tercera's own how-to guide states in-person applicants must bring a 'cedula de identidad vigente' (current ID card); atencionchilena.cl confirms Clave Unica is issued by the Servicio de Registro Civil e Identificacion specifically to foreigners with residence in Chile, against valid Chilean identity documentation - not a foreign passport.
dead_ends.condition: Foreigner without a Chilean ID card
dead_ends.common_misconception: That any government-issued photo ID, including a home-country passport, satisfies Chile's 'cedula de identidad vigente' requirement.

workarounds.action: Wait for the definitive Cedula de Identidad para Extranjeros to be issued by the Registro Civil, then request Clave Unica in person at a Civil Registry office or via a scheduled videoconference
workarounds.condition: Foreigner who already holds the definitive ID card

workarounds.action: Chileans and foreign residents abroad can request Clave Unica remotely through a Chilean consulate, scheduling a videoconference with Civil Registry officials instead of visiting an office in Chile
workarounds.condition: Applicant located outside Chile with a valid ID card
